daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka expressed his intention to resign to President Prabowo Subianto following the Supreme Court's decision to invalidate his high school diploma equivalency certificate. The government, through State Secretary Yusril Ihza Mahendra, assured there will be no vice presidential vacancy, while Gibran seeks to prove his diploma's validity through the State Administrative Court (PTUN). Former Constitutional Court Chief Justice Mahfud MD stated it would be more honorable for Gibran to resign than face impeachment, while legal expert Denny Indrayana criticized Gibran's PTUN move, saying he should resign instead.

  • The Supreme Court released six points of consideration explaining its decision to invalidate Gibran's high school diploma certificate.
  • PKB affirmed that the right to express opinion process against Gibran will continue despite his PTUN challenge, while a formal inquiry mechanism is being discussed in the DPR.
  • Hidayat Nur Wahid (HNW) resigned from his position as Deputy Speaker of the MPR, though he stated his resignation is unrelated to the Gibran controversy.
  • National Police Chief Suyudi withdrew two three-star generals from the Presidential Staff Office (KSP) and issued a new telegram reassigning 25 officers amid ongoing institutional changes.
  • A new development in the wiretapping scandal saw witnesses placed under protection and former presidential aide Ahrie Sonta dismissed from his position.
  • KPK deputy Fahd Arafiq acknowledged being questioned by the supervisory board regarding alleged document leaks in a land rights case.
  • Police Chief Suyudi and DPR Deputy Speaker Sufmi Dasco visited the Yogyakarta provincial parliament in the early hours following clashes during demonstrations, with the National Police Chief announcing he will investigate protesters who brought Molotov cocktails and sharp weapons.

Foreign Policy & Defence

A U.S. Deputy Secretary of State will visit Indonesia, Singapore, and Japan to strengthen technology partnerships in the region. Indonesia presented three priorities to halt deforestation at COP31 and highlighted five climate strategies at the conference pavilion.

  • Indonesia is fast-tracking reforms for 2028 OECD membership, accelerating institutional and policy adjustments to meet international standards.
  • Indonesian police arrested online scam suspects in the Philippines, marking a cross-border law enforcement operation against cybercrime.
  • Indonesia is courting Austrian investment for transport infrastructure development projects.

Other

Indonesia announced ambitious environmental targets, with the government targeting full waste management by 2029 and an end to open dumping practices nationwide. The government has prepared Rp883 billion in subsidies for the Christmas and New Year travel period to ease the burden on holiday travelers.

  • The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is intensifying global investor outreach amid ongoing market reforms to attract foreign capital.
  • Bank Syariah Indonesia reported that its Islamic KUR disbursement reached Rp10.4 trillion, achieving 69.4 percent of its annual target.
  • The KPK raided six locations in connection with a corruption case involving road projects in North Sumatra.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs announced it will strengthen civil servant investigators as Hajj and Umrah fraud cases increase, and ordered immediate raids on unlicensed Hajj and Umrah travel agencies.
  • Indonesia's data center capacity still lags behind Malaysia, highlighting infrastructure gaps in the digital economy sector.
